title: Mobile State Fixture v1
description: EPIC M2.01 of docs/plan/MOBILE-EPIC-M2-UNITS.md. Epic M2's objective is 'every critical journey starts from reproducible state'; this is the declared-state contract a fixture file must satisfy before M2.02's reset adapters, M2.03's test-only routes, or M2.05's provenance evidence can act on it. scripts/mobile_state_fixture.py is a read-only LOADER/VALIDATOR only: it checks a fixture file against this schema and a small set of hand rules the schema's keywords cannot express (see that module's docstring). It never resets device state, never talks to a simulator/emulator, and never talks to a backend -- that is M2.02's separate, later scope. Only the keyword subset scripts/mobile_project_profile.py and scripts/mobile_toolchain_probe.py already document is used here (same convention): type, required, properties, enum, const, items, minItems, additionalProperties -- no $ref/definitions, scripts/contract_check.py's enforced subset does not support them, confirmed by the M1.03 dispatch before this unit started, so every object is written out flat and in full below rather than referenced.

schema_version.description: Which shape this record follows, so a reader never has to guess.

fixture_id.description: A stable identifier for this fixture, e.g. 'onboarding-fresh-install-v1'. Never the founder's own priority app's real name (standing never-name-the-app rule); name it by role/journey instead.

account_data_ref.description: A reference/pointer to the account or data fixture a journey should start from (e.g. a fixture-store id or a file path under a fixtures directory). Never a real account's data inline -- this field only points at one, it does not carry one; scripts/mobile_state_fixture.py's hand_rules refuses a value that looks secret/PII-shaped (an email address, a live https:// endpoint, a 'password=' shape) as a cheap, non-exhaustive backstop.

backend_dataset.description: The backend-side dataset this fixture assumes, so a journey run against a fixture that has drifted from its backend counterpart fails loudly (wrong version) instead of silently.

id.description: Stable id of the backend dataset/namespace this fixture pairs with.

version.description: The dataset's own version/revision string. Compared by the caller, not by this schema, against whatever the backend actually reports.

app_storage.description: How the app's own local/on-device storage should be prepared before a journey starts. reset_mode picks one of three strategies; checkpoint_ref and preserved_keys are each required only for the strategy that needs them -- a conditional the keyword subset below cannot express, enforced instead by scripts/mobile_state_fixture.py's hand_rules (documented there).

reset_mode.description: 'clean': wipe all local app storage. 'restore-checkpoint': restore a previously captured snapshot named in checkpoint_ref. 'preserve-named-keys': wipe everything except the key names listed in preserved_keys.

checkpoint_ref.description: Reference to the snapshot/checkpoint to restore. Required (non-null) only when reset_mode is 'restore-checkpoint'; the exact snapshot format is M2.02's concern, not this schema's.

preserved_keys.description: Storage key names to leave untouched. Required (non-empty) only when reset_mode is 'preserve-named-keys'; ignored otherwise. minItems:1 is a schema-level backstop (the hand rule enforcing 'required' already rejects an empty list too).

keychain_policy.description: How keychain (iOS) / keystore (Android) entries should be prepared. Kept separate from app_storage because keychain/keystore survives an app uninstall on real devices in ways local storage does not -- conflating the two would hide that difference from a fixture author.

mode.description: 'clean': remove all entries this app owns. 'preserve': leave entries untouched. 'seeded': plant the entries named in seeded_items before the journey starts.

seeded_items.description: Names (never real secret values -- this is a reference list, the actual seed values live in whatever secret store M2.02's adapter reads; scripts/mobile_state_fixture.py's hand_rules also refuses a value that merely looks secret-shaped) of keychain/keystore entries to seed. Used only when mode is 'seeded'.

feature_flags.description: Flag name -> boolean toggle. Deliberately boolean-only (YAGNI): a flag needing a non-boolean value is a different, larger fixture concern than this unit's scope and can be added when a real journey needs it, not guessed at now.

clock.description: Whether the journey runs against a fixed, deterministic clock or the machine's real clock. fixed_value is required only when mode is 'fixed' -- enforced by hand_rules, not by the keywords below.

fixed_value.description: ISO-8601 timestamp the clock should report. Required (non-null) only when mode is 'fixed'.

randomness_seed.description: Seed for any deterministic-randomness hook (see M2.04). null means real/unseeded randomness -- an explicit choice, not an omission.

locale.description: Locale identifier the app/OS should report, e.g. 'en-US'.

timezone.description: IANA timezone id the device/simulator should report, e.g. 'Asia/Tokyo'.

network_profile.description: The network condition a journey should run under.

mode.description: 'throttled' covers any degraded-but-connected condition; detail names the exact profile (e.g. 'slow-3g') so 'throttled' does not have to grow a new enum value per condition.

detail.description: Profile name, meaningful only when mode is 'throttled' (e.g. 'slow-3g', 'high-latency'). Required (non-empty) when mode is 'throttled', forbidden otherwise -- enforced by hand_rules, not by the keywords below (an earlier draft of this schema let 'throttled' pass with no detail and let 'online' carry a silently-ignored detail; caught by Muse's adversarial review, 2026-09-15).

permissions.description: OS permission name (e.g. 'location', 'notifications', 'camera') -> the state it should be seeded to before the journey starts. 'prompt' means the OS should still be asking; 'not-determined' means never asked at all; 'limited' is iOS 14+'s reduced-access grant (e.g. selected-photos-only); 'restricted' is an OS/MDM-level block the user cannot themselves change (distinct from 'denied', which the user chose and can reverse). Extended past the original four-state draft after Muse's adversarial review (2026-09-15) named 'limited' as a real, commonly-tested iOS state this schema could not express.

location.description: Location-services state. latitude/longitude are required together when mode is 'simulated', forbidden otherwise, and range-checked (-90..90 / -180..180) -- all three enforced by hand_rules, not by the keywords below.

latitude.description: Degrees, -90..90. Required (non-null) only when mode is 'simulated'.

longitude.description: Degrees, -180..180. Required (non-null) only when mode is 'simulated'.

notifications.description: Push/local notification handling for the journey.

external_services.description: References to external-service sandbox configs the journey depends on (e.g. a payments sandbox, a maps sandbox). Never a live production service reference -- this fixture contract is a test-state contract, not a production config; scripts/mobile_state_fixture.py's hand_rules refuses an entry that looks like a live https:// endpoint or other secret-shaped value as a cheap, non-exhaustive backstop.

cleanup_policy.description: Whether cleanup after the journey is required, and how. method is required only when required is true -- enforced by hand_rules, not by the keywords below.

method.description: How cleanup should be performed (e.g. 'restore-checkpoint', 'delete-account', 'reset-app-storage'). Required (non-null) only when required is true.
